data.title: "The EDR Didn't Do It... Or Did It? A Comprehensive Guide to Defender for Endpoint Performance Analysis"

You'll see a live demonstration of how this tool can help you quickly identify bottlenecks, pinpoint problematic processes and gather the evidence you need to prove if your EDR is innocent or guilty.

Walk away from this session with practical skills, a proven troubleshooting methodology, and a new tool in your arsenal to tackle performance investigations with confidence.

data.title: A Tale of Two Kiosks: Assigned Access and Restricted User Access
data.abstract:
Certain verticals rely on Windows Kiosks heavily, like Retail, Manufacturing, and more. We see them daily when we go to retail stores or gas stations, because the value is huge.

There's more than just a standard kiosk setup. You can also deliver a more restricted user experience, which is a true art form.

Some of the common use-cases include:

PCs in public areas like hotels for printing flight info, etc.
PCs being used to ordered food or display a menu
POS (Point-of-Sale) systems
ThinPC-like platforms to lock into apps like Windows 365
Historically speaking, people would typically just use the Kiosk policy in Intune, but those days are mostly gone in Windows 11 with the continued expansion of capabilities to deliver better Kiosk experiences. Two of the ways you can deliver Kiosk are:

Assigned Access (lets you leverage a UWP app (WinGet apps) or Microsoft Edge in a full screen mode displaying an essential single-pane-of-glass.
Shell Launcher (lets you execute an application that replaces the default Windows UI/shell aka explorer, but it doesn’t actually run above the lock screen.
Multi-App Kiosk (also known as “restricted user experience”), which puts you into the desktop with a specified list of application. It’s based off the Assigned Access design.

data.title: Azure Virtual Desktop at Scale: Why Your Landing Zone Matters More Than You Think
data.abstract:
Many organizations jump into Azure Virtual Desktop to solve an end-user computing challenge, but quickly run into issues that are not AVD problems at all. AVD is deployed, but the Azure foundation underneath was never designed for it.

In this session, we step back and focus on what really makes AVD successful: a scalable and secure Azure foundation. I will explain how enterprise environments design Azure Landing Zones that properly support Azure Virtual Desktop, covering identity, network design, management structure, governance, and security baselines. Without this foundation, AVD environments often grow in an uncontrolled way, leading to operational overhead, security risks, and costly redesigns later.

We will look at common patterns seen in real customer environments, including setups that started small, for example with a Cloud Management Gateway or a few workloads, and evolved into complex environments with public exposure, excessive permissions, and missing governance. I will show how to identify these gaps using automation and assessments, and how to move toward a structured Landing Zone model that supports AVD at scale.

This session is based on real-world experience from Azure security assessments and Landing Zone implementations, with a strong focus on making AVD environments sustainable, secure, and ready for growth.

data.title: Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid – What Does It Mean and How to Get Started
data.abstract:
Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) has become Microsoft’s flagship solution for desktop virtualization — and its evolution is far from over. While today AVD typically requires session hosts to be provisioned either in Azure or on Azure Local, the next step introduces a major shift: running AVD session hosts on virtually any hypervisor, such as Hyper-V, outside of Azure.
 
This hybrid capability is particularly compelling for organizations facing latency challenges to backend systems hosted in on-premises datacenters, where running desktops natively in Azure is not yet feasible. It also opens new possibilities for reusing existing hypervisor investments without first embarking on an Azure Local project. In addition, regulatory or compliance requirements — such as keeping data within a private datacenter — often make a hybrid approach essential.
 
But how does Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid actually work? How can session hosts be created and managed — ideally in an automated way — without relying on the Azure VM control plane? What architectural considerations, limitations, and use cases should you be aware of?
In this session, we will explore the fundamentals of Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid, explain the underlying concepts, and walk through practical first steps to get started. Attendees will gain a clear understanding of when and why this new deployment model makes sense, and how to approach it in real-world scenarios.

data.title: Deletion Happens – Are You Ready for Recovery in Entra ID?
data.abstract:
Backup and restore have always been fundamental principles of IT, yet in Microsoft Entra ID, they are often misunderstood, underestimated, or simply ignored.

What happens when a Conditional Access policy is modified and you suddenly need last week’s configuration?
What can actually be restored in Entra ID and what is permanently lost?

In this session, we take a deep dive into deletion and recovery behavior across different Entra resource types, from identities and groups to Conditional Access policies and tenant-wide configurations. We separate myths from reality and clarify where restoration is technically possible and where it simply isn’t.

A key focus will be the new Unified Tenant Configuration Management (UTCM) capability, released in January 2026, and how it fundamentally changes configuration governance. You’ll see how UTCM enables administrators to track, compare, and safeguard tenant-wide settings — shifting the conversation from reactive recovery to proactive configuration control.

The goal is simple: to provide clarity, eliminate assumptions, and help you design a realistic protection strategy for your Entra ID environment, without relying solely on third-party backup solutions.

Misconfigurations, overlapping policies, and unclear assignment strategies can quickly lead to inconsistent results, user impact, and operational complexity.

In this session, Kenneth will share practical guidance on how to design and implement Intune compliance policies in a structured and scalable way. We will explore when to use a single policy versus multiple policies, how assignments and filters determine policy targeting, and how compliance state is evaluated and reported on the endpoint.

The session also covers how compliance policies interact with Conditional Access, and how design decisions directly influence access outcomes. In addition, we will look at common troubleshooting scenarios and how to identify and resolve issues when devices do not report or evaluate compliance as expected.

Based on real-world implementations, this session provides actionable design patterns and operational insights that help you move from basic configuration to a controlled and maintainable compliance strategy.

After this session, you will have a clear understanding of how to design, assign, and operate compliance policies in a way that supports both security and usability in modern Microsoft 365 environments.

Modern compliance requires real-time, automated responses to ever-changing risks. In this deep-dive session, we’ll explore how to build event-driven architectures around Microsoft Purview using the Azure Platform.

We’ll cover advanced scenarios such as chaining Purview events into multi-step workflows, integrating with security operations tools, applying conditional logic for policy enforcement, and building resilient, reusable automation patterns.

Designed for architects and advanced practitioners, this session focuses on practical implementation strategies, design considerations, and lessons learned from the field.

data.title: Every Device Is a Security Boundary: Secure It by Design
data.abstract:
In this hands-on, demo-driven session, you’ll learn how to take full ownership of your identity control plane using Microsoft Entra ID - with focus on devices. The focus is practical and actionable, with ready-to-use scripts and configurations you can bring back and implement immediately.

We’ll explore how to design and operate modern identity security by breaking down real-world security profiles such as Enterprise (ENT), Secure Access Workstations (SAW), and Privileged Access Workstations (PAW). You’ll gain a clear understanding of authentication strengths, methods, and why strong authentication is critical across different device types.

The session walks through how to build and secure PAW and SAW environments across Windows 365 Cloud PCs, virtual machines, and physical devices. You’ll see how to implement phishing-resistant authentication using FIDO2 and Windows Hello for Business across multiple device configurations, and how to classify and tag devices based on security posture and authentication capabilities.

We’ll also cover how to redesign your Microsoft Intune environment using device tags and filters to simplify management, enforce security boundaries, and reduce complexity. From there, we’ll dive into reporting and hunting techniques that help you identify, track, and remediate non-compliant devices at scale.

Finally, you’ll see how full automation can transform identity security, including how to implement and manage a large set of conditional access policies for consistent, enforceable control.

This session challenges outdated identity practices and shows how modern, automated identity design can improve both security and operational efficiency. If you want to move from manual processes to a scalable, resilient identity control plane, this session will put you firmly in the driver’s seat.

data.title: From Prompt to Playbook: Automating SOC Response with AI in Microsoft Sentinel
data.abstract:

In this session, we’ll explore how to use natural language to generate fully functional, code-based playbooks—transforming how security teams design and deploy automation. Powered by Microsoft Security Copilot, the playbook generator enables you to describe your intent and automatically produce Python-based workflows, complete with documentation and visual flow diagrams.

We’ll go beyond the basics and dive into advanced scenarios, including integration with external systems, enrichment pipelines, and decision-driven automation. You’ll learn how to design effective prompts, validate generated logic, and operationalize playbooks at scale using automation rules.

By the end of this session, you’ll understand how to shift from manual SOAR engineering to AI-assisted automation design, while still maintaining control, governance, and reliability.

data.title: From SCCM to Azure Arc: Lessons from Real Customer Projects

data.title: Patching in the Era of AI
data.abstract: The pace of vulnerability discovery is changing. Advances in AI make it possible to find more issues, faster, across more code, and the fastest way to reduce exposure is to find and fix those issues before attackers can use them. That's reshaping what "patched" needs to mean. This session goes under the hood on how Windows is evolving vulnerability management to meet the speed of AI-powered discovery: finding issues earlier and at greater scale, compressing the path from discovery to a validated, high-quality fix, and helping customers safely stay current without choosing between speed and stability. We'll show how modern update technologies like hotpatch, optional preview releases, and Known Issue Rollback keep protection flowing with less disruption, and how Windows Autopatch brings it all together in practice: automating security, driver, and firmware updates across rings, pausing on reliability signals, and surfacing where your estate is exposed. You'll leave with practical guidance for protecting your estate in the era of AI.

Whether you're modernizing your image lifecycle or preparing your environment for enterprise-scale VDI, this session will provide you with practical tips, key considerations to avoid, and real-world guidance to elevate your image strategy.

data.title: Implementing PAW without making everyone hate you*
data.abstract:
Privileged Access Workstations (PAW) tend to be one of the most overlooked parts of an enterprise security strategy, despite them being the most critical part of adhering to the clean source principle. And for a good share of organizations, they implement something that feels like PAW, but is it really? Or is it just security theater? We know anecdotally that most pushback is due to the perceived impact on work, and the culture change necessary with PAW.

But does it really have to hurt?

In this session we’ll explore many of the diametrically opposed scenarios that can hamper a good PAW implementation, and how to think about them and measure your own risk tolerance – admins needing to share screens and use tools like VS Code while we want to limit lateral movement and supply chain attacks. Limiting internet access on devices that, well, need to access the internet. And the culture part – we’ll talk about that too. Strategies for minimizing impact on productivity and behavioral changes, derived from real-world experience implementing PAW in an enterprise.

(* 100% no hate results not guaranteed, but we’ll try our best to minimize it)

data.abstract:
Modern automation in Intune, Entra, and Azure often depends on certificates and secrets, which are still frequently hardcoded in scripts or pipelines. This session focuses on the core security principles for safe automation, including identity‑first design, least privilege, and proper secret and certificate lifecycle management.
Using Azure Managed Identities and Azure Key Vault, we present a practical automation pattern that removes embedded secrets while enabling secure access to Intune and Azure APIs. The Azure Certificate & Secret Proxy serves as a real‑world example, showing how sensitive material can be centrally managed and consumed by automation without direct exposure.

data.title: Less Console, More Outcome: Agentic Administration for the Workplace
data.abstract: For twenty years the workplace admin's job has had the same shape: something breaks, a signal appears somewhere, you correlate it by hand, and you fix it, usually after the user has already noticed. AI does not remove that loop, but it is starting to collapse the middle of it. This 15 minute session looks technically at what that means in practice: where a model genuinely shortens the path from detection to root cause to remediation, and where it just adds a confident-sounding layer of guesswork. We will walk the loop end to end, from an anomaly on an endpoint, through automated triage, to an agentic action that actually changes state on the device, and be honest about the parts that are production-ready today versus the parts that are still a demo.

In addition, we'll break down the most impactful WWDC 2026 announcements and what they mean for you, including Intune's adoption of new capabilities such as allow/deny binaries and all the new settings. Whether you're planning a migration to Intune, modernizing an existing Mac deployment, or simply looking to stay ahead of the latest Apple and Intune innovations, you'll leave with practical guidance, a few demos, and a clear roadmap.

data.title: Mastering App Attach in Azure Virtual Desktop – Evolution, Architecture & Enterprise Implementation (Level 400)
data.abstract:

What started as a promising way to decouple applications from the base image has matured into a scalable solution for modern End User Computing environments.
In this Level 400 deep dive, Microsoft MVP Thomas Poppelgaard walks through how App Attach has evolved and how organizations can successfully design, implement, and operate App Attach at scale.
The session begins by exploring the evolution of App Attach over the past five years, highlighting improvements in MSIX tooling, storage performance, and Azure Virtual Desktop platform capabilities.
From there, the session dives deep into the technical architecture and operational best practices, including:
MSIX packaging and application preparation
Certificate management and signing best practices
Choosing between CIM and VHDX formats and when to use each
Storage architecture and performance considerations
Host pool integration and application publishing
Enterprise deployment models from development → test → production
You will also learn real-world troubleshooting techniques and lessons learned from enterprise deployments, helping you avoid common pitfalls when implementing App Attach.
If you want to understand how App Attach works under the hood and how to build a reliable and scalable application delivery platform in Azure Virtual Desktop, this session is for you.

data.title: My Cloud PC Feels Faster Than My Laptop — Let’s Talk About Why
data.abstract:
Cloud PCs often feel faster than the laptops on a user’s desk, and the reason is not a mystery. Microsoft has spent years innovating in global network design, transport optimisation and edge placement to create an experience that feels immediate, smooth and consistently high performing. This session reveals how those innovations work and why they matter.

Attendees will explore the network architecture that powers Cloud PCs, including Microsoft’s private backbone, Azure’s high bandwidth design, multipath routing, modern transport protocols and a worldwide footprint of gateways and TURN relays positioned close to users. These capabilities shorten paths, reduce round trip time and deliver a level of responsiveness that physical devices cannot achieve on consumer Wi‑Fi or ISP networks.

The session highlights how Microsoft has pushed the boundaries of remoting performance through protocol improvements, intelligent routing and strategic placement of access points across the globe. It explains how Cloud PCs benefit from proximity to Microsoft 365 services, how traffic stays on private fibre for most of its journey and how multipath connectivity keeps sessions smooth even when conditions vary.

If you want to understand why Cloud PCs feel fast, why they stay fast and how Microsoft has engineered a network that turns distance into an advantage, this session provides the full story. You will leave with a clear view of the innovation behind the experience and the breadth of capabilities that make Cloud PCs stand out.

data.title: Proactive Approach to Security Posture Management
data.abstract: : In today's rapidly evolving digital landscape, organizations face an increasing number of security threats that require a proactive and comprehensive approach to manage their security posture effectively. We will explore the challenges posed by siloed security defenses and the importance of contextual prioritization based on insights. The presentation will highlight the significance of cloud data security, the impact of misconfigurations, and the evolving landscape of vulnerability management. Attendees will gain insights into continuous threat exposure management, the role of AI in threat-informed defense, and the benefits of adopting an attacker's viewpoint to minimize the attack surface. Join us to learn how to strengthen your organization's security posture and protect against the ever-growing threat landscape.

data.title: Prove it worked: Intune reporting, latency, and the data platform
data.abstract:
Every day, IT administrators deploy applications, enforce compliance policies, apply configurations, remove software, and collect inventory across thousands of devices. But after taking action, they are left with the same question: Did it work? 

Trust in device management depends on trust in the data. When reporting is delayed, incomplete, or difficult to interpret, administrators are forced to guess whether actions succeeded, troubleshoot without evidence, and make decisions with limited confidence. 

In this session, we'll explore how Microsoft is helping Intune administrators move from assumptions to evidence. We'll walk through investments in deployment latency and inventory reporting, including Fast Notify channels, App Inventory reporting, data freshness indicators, and significant reductions in end-to-end reporting latency. We'll also cover advances in Custom Inventory that enable organizations to collect and report on registry and file-based data that has historically been difficult to track at scale. 

Beyond individual features, we'll examine the data platform improvements that make trusted and timely reporting possible, and why reliable evidence is becoming the foundation for operational insights, troubleshooting, and AI-assisted management experiences. 

Join us to learn how Intune is helping administrators answer one of the most important questions in device management: "I asked Intune to do something, can I prove it worked?"

data.title: Questions your CISO is asking about security for AI and how to answer them
data.abstract:
Generative AI agents are rapidly becoming part of everyday work, but for IT and Security teams they introduce a new set of questions: What AI agents are running in my environment? What can they access? How do I control them without breaking productivity? How do I protect users and data when agents act on their behalf?
This session explores how Microsoft Intune helps you confidently answer these questions and more using built-in capabilities to observe, govern, and secure local AI agents on your managed devices. Attendees will learn how to gain visibility into local AI agents discovered on managed devices; govern agent usage through execution policies, Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), and runtime protections; and enable restrictions to protect against unwanted Shadow AI. 
Through real-world security scenarios and common CISO questions, we will show how a layered AI security strategy can help provide visibility, compliance, control, and protection. As AI agents become increasingly autonomous and capable of acting on behalf of users, traditional app management and security controls are no longer sufficient. You will leave this session with a practical framework for managing the agents you can control, restricting the ones you can’t, and building layers of security to keep your enterprise safe as generative AI continues to rapidly evolve.

data.title: Rethinking the Endpoint: The Forces Reshaping How We Manage and Secure Work
data.abstract: The way we manage and secure endpoints is being rewritten in real time. Tighter budgets and rising expectations, a growing sprawl of devices and user choice, AI shifting from experiment to everyday, and a fresh look at vulnerability management are colliding at once. In this opening keynote, we cut through the noise to name the trends that matter, separate signal from hype, and connect what you're seeing in your own org to what's happening across the industry. The aim is practical: get the fundamentals right, know where AI genuinely helps, and leave with a clear picture of how it all fits together — and which of the summit's sessions to dig into next.

On the Android side, we'll explore the latest Intune innovations, including the transition to the Android Management API, new web-based enrollment experiences for work profile devices, expanded Android Enterprise controls, direct management of line-of-business Android applications, enhanced credential provider support, and new security capabilities such as Strict Tunnel Mode. 
Throughout the session, we'll focus on practical guidance for provisioning corporate devices faster, strengthening security without sacrificing usability, and taking advantage of the newest Intune capabilities released over the past year. data.title: The Hidden Risks in Your Entra Tenant – A Housekeeping Guide

These leftover objects often go unnoticed — yet they quietly expand the attack surface.

In this session, I walk through practical Entra ID housekeeping: which abandoned objects typically accumulate, why they are a real security concern, and how to reliably identify them. I demonstrate real-world techniques using logs, PowerShell, and Security Copilot to gain visibility and clean up effectively.

You will leave with a clear and actionable checklist to streamline your tenant, reduce risk, and maintain long-term security and clarity in your directory — with no zombies left hiding in your tenant.

data.title: Your Next Enrollment Doesn't Have to Be a Black Box
data.abstract:
An Autopilot enrollment is a black box. It either finishes, or it doesn't - and when it doesn't, you're left with a user who says "it took forever", an ESP screen nobody screenshotted, and IME logs on a device that has since been wiped. Everything you know is what you can reconstruct after the fact.

I've always enjoyed troubleshooting Autopilot. But I'll be honest about why: because I know where to look. That's a bad reason for something to be enjoyable - it means answering "why did this enrollment fail?" is locked behind years of log-reading experience. This session is
about taking those troubleshooting approaches out of people's heads and putting them into something everyone can use.

What becomes possible when you watch an enrollment while it happens: 200+ different signals per session in near real time, a detailed event timeline, automatic diagnostics collection at the moment things break, and analysis rules that tell you why an enrollment failed instead of just that it failed. On top of that: fleet health reporting across all your deployments, a progress
portal your end users can actually watch, and delegated-admin support for MSPs managing many tenants.

We'll go one step further and connect the data to an AI assistant over MCP - a structured way to ask questions of your enrollment telemetry instead of grepping logs by hand.

data.title: The MSP Challenge of Microsoft 365 Security at Scale
data.abstract:
Managing Microsoft 365 security at in one tenant can be a challenge. Scaling that to hundreds seems impossible.

Every change to Entra ID, Intune, Defender, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Purview and Copilot introduces the potential for drift. Security standards become inconsistent, configurations diverge, and operational overhead grows as engineers spend more time auditing, comparing and remediating environments.

In this session, we'll explore the challenges of maintaining consistency across Microsoft 365 and why traditional point-in-time assessments fail to keep pace with continuously changing tenants. You'll see practical approaches for identifying configuration drift, enforcing standards, and delivering continuous assurance across every workload, without relying on scripts, spreadsheets or manual reviews.

Whether you're managing ten or hundreds of customer tenants, you'll leave with an understanding of how inforcer gives you strategies for reducing risk, increasing operational efficiency and bringing consistency back to Microsoft 365 security management.

Expect survey insights, real scenarios, and a practical, technical look at what modern user profile management actually looks like in 2026.

data.title: What’s Next After Phishing-Resistant MFA? Securing the Post-Authentication Attack Surface
data.abstract:
Over the past decade, identity security has gone through multiple waves of innovation. We moved from username and password to multi-factor authentication, and more recently to phishing-resistant MFA to defend against adversary-in-the-middle attacks.

But eliminating phishing does not eliminate identity compromise.

Attackers are shifting their focus to what happens after authentication. Techniques such as token theft, session hijacking, and device compromise allow adversaries to bypass even the strongest authentication methods and reuse valid sessions on other systems.

In this session, we explore the next phase of identity security and what it means for Microsoft 365 environments. We will look at how attackers operate beyond authentication and how to defend against these scenarios using capabilities such as device binding, Conditional Access, Continuous Access Evaluation, token protection, and endpoint detection and response.

You will learn how to reduce the risk of token replay, how to enforce stronger ties between identity and device, and how to detect and respond to post-authentication threats in real-world environments.

After this session, you will have a clear understanding of where identity security is heading and what practical steps you can take to stay ahead of modern attack techniques.

My normal conference sessions tend to live somewhere between Level 500 Windows internals and stand-up comedy — and some of them have even won Best Session awards. This time, with beer involved, I see absolutely no reason to lower the risk.

Come for the Windows history. Stay for the stories.

data.title: Zero Trust: From Buzzword to Action
data.abstract:
Every organisation knows Zero Trust by now.
The three principles are on every slide deck, the six pillars are in every framework, and the Microsoft tooling is already licensed.
Yet most tenants still run with half-configured policies, standing admin access, and trust assumptions that attackers exploit daily.
The gap is not awareness. The gap is knowing what to do, with what tool, and who should own it.

Cloud Security MVP Pouyan Khabazi starts with why Zero Trust matters and what it really means, then goes pillar by pillar through the practical implementation.

This session walks through all six Zero Trust pillars with a consistent structure for each one.
What to configure — the concrete actions and quick wins that make a real difference.
What Microsoft product is needed — the exact technology and license level required.
Who owns it — which team or role is responsible, because Zero Trust without ownership fails.
What changes — the mindset shift from the old way of working to how Zero Trust changes your decisions.

Every pillar comes with real configuration examples from production environments and clear guidance on where to start.
You will leave with a complete picture of what Zero Trust looks like when it is actually implemented, not just discussed.

This is technical and built for people who manage Microsoft 365 and Azure in production today.
No marketing slides, only configurations that work and decisions that matter.
Slides are shared afterwards with ready-to-use action steps per pillar for your team.
Join and walk out ready to implement Zero Trust the right way.
